about: Floods series, FINAL DRAFT rc3 (1.0.0-rc3): every word the sheets print, with its sources. Written by tools/floods/rc1/notes.py; read by tools/floods/rc1/sheet.py. `checked` says how far a source carries a line. Written with Claude for Chris Busse.

sources.rain-events: drafts/richmond-floods/casestudy/2026-11-23-03-research-gaston-and-the-weather/sources.md: S20 (Style Weekly, quoting the weather service: the first flash-flood warning, 3:58 p.m.), S5 (NCEI Storm Events: flash flooding begins 4:30; the file labels its times EST, and whether that means standard time, so 5:30 p.m. EDT, is not confirmed; hence "about 4:30, flooding reported"), S18 (the 2009 lawsuit alleges flooding by 4:30), S23 (AP via Insurance Journal: a car afloat in the Bottom about 6:30), S10 and S12 (USGS 02037500 Westham: peak 14,800 cfs at 9:15 p.m.); Storm Events times are labeled EST in the file, so they may be an hour late (tools/floods/rain/figures.py on feature/flood-rain)

shockoe:1771:1788.title: The flood of 1771, an estimate, on the town of about 1788
lines: Water at about 38 ft above sea level (NAVD88) at the City Locks, derived from a 1771 stage of 38 ft on the old gauge near Mayo's Bridge (the Corps, from diaries); other accounts give 30 ft and 45 ft on unstated bases; ±3 ft is our judgment. Hatched: up to 41 ft.
231.5 acres under water off the channel; buildings in the water: 1 of the 6 shown (3.7 ft median, 3.7 ft deepest).
Bathtub fill, not a flood model, on today's ground; the town of 1788 as the downtown history draws it: few of its buildings are known. FINAL DRAFT rc3.
shockoe:1771:1788.checked: Level and its range from levels.json; counts from the build (scene stats); "not ascertained" and "left out" from the evidence layer and the stated rules (how-its-made, Floods).

Its dry twin: the same city with no flood, the same ground, wall and buildings, to compare.
Bathtub fill, not a flood model. Today's city; the flats' earthen levee is not mapped. FINAL DRAFT rc3.
manchester:agnes-today-nowall-dry:2026.checked: Level and its range from levels.json; counts from the build (scene stats); "not ascertained" and "left out" from the evidence layer and the stated rules (how-its-made, Floods).

manchester:1996-dry:2026.title: Hurricane Fran's height (September 1996) against today's wall
lines: Water at 22.7 ft above sea level (NAVD88) at the City Locks (weather service crest record), perhaps 1 ft more (hatched); perhaps 1 ft higher at the Mayo Bridge (assumed from 1969).
Its dry twin: the same city with no flood, the same ground, wall and buildings, to compare.

Bathtub fill, not a flood model. Today's city; the flats' earthen levee is not mapped. Wall top: the 41 ft stage at which the weather service says the wall is overtopped, not surveyed. FINAL DRAFT rc3.
manchester:1996-dry:2026.checked: Level and its range from levels.json; counts from the build (scene stats); "not ascertained" and "left out" from the evidence layer and the stated rules (how-its-made, Floods).

manchester:2020-dry:2026.title: The November 2020 height against today's wall
lines: Water at 17.0 ft above sea level (NAVD88) at the City Locks (±0.1 ft; USGS gauge record), held level, with no rise assumed toward the Mayo Bridge. The weather service puts the treatment plant's access road, Maury to Brander Street, under water at 18.5 ft.
Its dry twin: the same city with no flood, the same ground, wall and buildings, to compare.

Bathtub fill, not a flood model. Today's city; the flats' earthen levee is not mapped. Wall top: the 41 ft stage at which the weather service says the wall is overtopped, not surveyed. FINAL DRAFT rc3.

market.title: 17th Street Market
market.note: Beside it lies the Bottom's lowest point on the lidar, a pit at 13.4 ft; water stood here in every river flood drawn before the wall.
market.checked: rc2 (fact 5): "the lowest ground of the Bottom" was too strong (box 3's center is lower); the pit is step 15's low point (4.07 m, 13.4 ft), beside the market. "Every river flood drawn before the wall": 1936, 1969, 1972, 1985 in this drawing (counts.json rc2).

station.title: Main Street Station and its train shed
station.note: Camille's mapped water (USGS) reached about this far up the valley.
station.checked: HA-410 as read in floods.md ("up to about Main Street Station").

dock.title: 17th and Dock, the canal's end
dock.note: Buried Shockoe Creek runs south under the valley to 17th and Dock; today the wall's 17th Street closure crosses Dock Street here.
dock.checked: rc2 (fact 10): the source says the creek "runs south from north of I-64 to 17th and Dock" (S35); "reaches the James" was an inference.

slip.title: Shockoe Slip, 14th and Cary
slip.note: Where the water's edge meets the rise to downtown.
slip.checked: A statement about the drawing, true on 1969, 1972 and 1985 (the water's edge crosses the box: 0.5, 3.7 and 1.3 acres wet, counts.json rc3); 1936 has its own note.

canal.title: The canal at Virginia and Byrd streets
canal.note: The canal's riverfront: in the water in every river flood drawn before the wall; behind its west end (12th and Byrd) since.
canal.checked: Wet in 1936, 1969, 1972 and 1985 and dry behind the wall in 1996, 2020 and at the 1972 height today, in this drawing (counts.json rc2); the wall runs from 12th and Byrd to 21st and East Cary (City FAQ, floodwall.md). Names from OSM.

cary18.title: 18th and Cary streets
cary18.note: Warehouses between Cary and Dock streets, in the water in every river flood drawn here before the wall.
cary18.checked: rc2 (fact 8): "Tobacco Row's west end" had no source and is dropped. A count of this drawing.

franklin.title: East Franklin and Grace, 17th to 19th
franklin.note: The 1980 National Register survey dates the Franklin Street row, 1703 to 1721, from about 1842 (the Anson Richards houses) to about 1950.
franklin.checked: rc2 (fact 1): rc1 said "from 1842 to 1913"; the survey extract has 1705 at about 1930 and 1718 at about 1950 (step 44).

g-market.title: 17th Street Market and Havana '59 (pins A, B)
g-market.note: A: most of the water came together at 17th and Main (Washington Post). B: Havana '59, at its usual address: water 13 ft up the dining-room wall, by the owner's account; on the lidar's 18 ft ground that is about 31 ft, in the hatch.
g-market.checked: Ground at the pin from the 2 m lidar: 18.4 ft; 18.4 + 13 = 31.4 ft. The address is the business's usual one, not stated in the source (gaston-water.md, section 2).

g-dock.title: Bottoms Up, 17th and Dock (pin C)
g-dock.note: C: Bottoms Up, at its usual address: "6 ft 2 in inside, above a 3 ft step" (the owner, NBC12), about 9 ft over the street; on the lidar's 18 ft ground that is about 27 ft, as drawn.
g-dock.checked: The source's own words; ground at the pin 18.2 ft (2 m lidar); 18.2 + 9.2 = 27.4 ft.

g-station.title: 15th and Main, Main Street Station (pins D, E)
g-station.note: D: "rapids" at 15th and Main (a developer, WTVR). E: Main Street Station escaped damage (Washington Post), though still water at 28 ft would stand about 3 ft at its door: the water ran through here and did not stand at one level.
g-station.checked: Ground at pin E 25.2 ft (2 m lidar), so 2.8 ft under a 28 ft level; the reports and a level surface do not agree here, and the note says so.

g-valley.title: The valley above: 17th Street to Franklin
g-valley.note: Runoff from Church Hill and the Capitol slope ran into the Bottom (AP); here the hatch reaches the reports' upper figure, 35 ft.
g-valley.checked: S22 (Insurance Journal, AP, Sept. 20, 2004): runoff off Church Hill and the Capitol slope into the Bottom.

w-dock.title: 17th and Dock, the wall's Dock Street closure

w-canal.title: The canal at Virginia and Byrd, the wall's west end
w-canal.note: The north wall begins at 12th and Byrd; west of its end the canal's riverfront is open to the river.
w-canal.checked: City FAQ via floodwall.md (12th and Byrd to 21st and East Cary).

w-shiplock.title: Great Shiplock Park, past the wall's east end
w-shiplock.note: The north wall ends at 21st and East Cary; past it the park and the canal's lock lie open to the river.
w-shiplock.checked: City FAQ via floodwall.md; names from OSM.

hull.title: Hull Street at the Mayo Bridge
hull.note: The bridge's south foot, inside the wall: dry with it at the 1972 height, deep without.

flats.title: The flats at 5th and Stockton
flats.note: Warehouses and shops on the flats; USGS mapped Camille's water across them to about Commerce Road.
flats.checked: HA-410 as read in floods.md, "What flooded".

tanks.title: The tank farm
tanks.note: Fuel storage tanks on the flats (as OSM tags them), behind the wall.

wall.title: On the wall
wall.note: Just west of the Mayo Bridge the wall is a gravity U-wall, 43 ft from its top to the river's edge (City FAQ).
wall.checked: rc2 (fact 6): "its tallest part" dropped; rc3 (F2): "Just west", the FAQ's place.

plant.title: The treatment plant grounds
plant.note: The 1986 law says the project "shall include flood protection for the Richmond municipal wastewater treatment facility"; our map data cannot show the levee, so with the wall this ground is drawn as not known.

key.label: Water, by depth (ft)
key.means: palette.ts flood tones; depth = the flood's level less the 5 m ground grid (the gauges and the boxes' figures read the 2 m lidar at their place)

key.label: The river, canal and basins at their own level
key.means: the lidar's water surface, in the flood look's channel color on every flood sheet

key.label: Hatched: the range of an estimate
key.means: the flood's level to the top of its stated range (1771 ±3 ft; Fran +1 ft; Gaston 28 to 35 ft)

key.label: Cross-hatched: not known; the earthen levee is not mapped (the edges assume where it runs)
key.means: land the with-wall fill reaches only because the levee is not in our data (flood.ts `unknown`); no water and no depth are drawn there; its edges follow the two lines assumed for the levee's course (floods.py UNKNOWN)

key.label: A building of the year
key.means: standing that year by year built, traced maps or air photos

key.label: A building standing in 1788 (by its year built)
key.means: today's buildings dated before 1788, and curated ones, as the downtown history draws them

key.label: Grey, dashed roof edge: on an earlier map or photo, not ascertained for the year
The floodwall (1994), where it stands
key.means: dedicated October 21, 1994; its top drawn at the 41 ft stage at which the weather service says the wall is overtopped, not a surveyed top

key.label: A bridge deck under the water (deck heights are estimates)
key.means: a deck piece whose deck, at its middle, lies below the water: drawn faintly on the surface. Deck heights are the region's rules over the ground or river, not surveys

key.label: A depth gauge, the figure in feet
key.means: the flood's level less the 2 m lidar at the place

key.label: Lettered pins: places named in reports
key.means: pins at 17th and Main, 16 N. 17th St., 1700 Dock St., 15th and Main and the station; the two addresses are the businesses' usual ones, not stated in the sources (gaston-water.md, section 2)

key.label: Dry twin: the same city with no flood
key.means: every plate has a pixel-aligned twin with the water taken away

rain.title: The rain over the land that drains to the Bottom, by hour
events: about 6:30 a car afloat in the Bottom
9:15 the James peaks, far below flood
rain.caption: About 10 inches of rain (8.6 to 11.6 by the estimates) fell on the 12 square miles that drain to Shockoe Bottom, most of it between 2 and 9 p.m., while the James stayed far below flood. Gaston was a tropical depression over Richmond while the rain fell (National Hurricane Center). Bars: the hourly average over the watershed; whiskers: the range of estimates.
rain.source: Rain: NEXRAD radar (NOAA, Wakefield) corrected to rain gauges (NCEI), averaged over the watershed from USGS 3DEP; computed for this series with Claude. Times: the weather service warning, NCEI Storm Events, AP, USGS (Westham gauge).
rain.checked: Numbers copied from tools/floods/rain/data/rain.json on feature/flood-rain (basin_hourly radar_corrected, low, high; basin_total 10.34, low 8.56, high 11.6; watershed 31.49 sq km). Event times as the rain branch's hyetograph gives them (figures.py EVENTS).
